--- title: "5 · Validation" --- ::: {.cell} ::: This page continues from steps 2 and 3. One line loads the data and builds the library: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r source("R/pipeline.R") ``` ## Python ```python from pipeline import * ``` ::: ## Solution The fitted equation is solved with a standard ODE solver: `deSolve::ode` (LSODA) in R and `scipy.integrate.solve_ivp` (LSODA) in Python. All years are integrated in one call, each with its own coefficients. The solver needs the drivers at arbitrary times. Biomass is recorded at the end of a day, so the weather of day $j$ drives the interval between observations $j-1$ and $j$. With $t$ counted from the first observation, the value of day $j$ is placed in the middle of that interval, $t = j - \tfrac{3}{2}$, and values in between are interpolated linearly. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r ## Solves dy/dt = (1, theta(y, u)) coef. coef: year x (1 + terms), U: year ## x day x variable. terms(y, u) is the library; by default U is the library. simulate <- function(coef, U, y0, terms = function(y, u) u, method = "lsoda") { S <- dim(U)[1]; D <- dim(U)[2] days <- lapply(seq_len(D), function(j) matrix(U[, j, ], S)) b0 <- coef[, 1]; B <- coef[, -1, drop = FALSE] rhs <- function(t, y, parms) { pos <- min(max(t + 0.5, 0), D - 1) # day j is placed at time j - 3/2 j <- min(floor(pos), D - 2) w <- pos - j # linear interpolation between days u <- (1 - w) * days[[j + 1]] + w * days[[j + 2]] list(b0 + .rowSums(terms(y, u) * B, S, ncol(B))) } deSolve::ode(y0, 0:(D - 1), rhs, NULL, method = method, rtol = 1e-4, atol = 1e-4)[, -1, drop = FALSE] } ``` ## Python ```python # Solves dy/dt = (1, theta(y, u)) coef. coef: year x (1 + terms), U: year # x day x variable. terms(y, u) is the library; by default U is the library. def simulate(coef, U, y0, terms=lambda y, u: u, method="LSODA"): D = U.shape[1] def rhs(t, y): pos = min(max(t + 0.5, 0.0), D - 1.0) # day j is placed at time j - 3/2 j = min(int(pos), D - 2) w = pos - j # linear interpolation u = (1 - w) * U[:, j] + w * U[:, j + 1] return coef[:, 0] + np.einsum("sk,sk->s", terms(y, u), coef[:, 1:]) return solve_ivp(rhs, (0, D - 1), y0, method=method, t_eval=np.arange(D), rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4).y ``` ::: If a library depends on the state, `terms(y, u)` is evaluated along the solution; by default the library depends on the drivers only. ## Leave-one-year-out cross-validation Each genotype has trajectories in the years $E$. A year $e$ is predicted by a model that has not seen it: $$ \begin{array}{ll} \textbf{for each genotype } g, \textbf{ for each year } e \in E: & \\[2pt] \quad \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}^{(-e)} \leftarrow \texttt{fit}\bigl(\mathbf{X}^{(-e)},\, \dot{\mathbf{y}}^{(-e)}\bigr) & \text{fit on the other years} \\[2pt] \quad \bar{y}_0^{(-e)} \leftarrow \tfrac{1}{|E|-1} \textstyle\sum_{e' \ne e} y_0^{(e')} & \text{mean initial biomass} \\[2pt] \quad \dfrac{d\hat y}{dt} = \boldsymbol{\theta}\bigl(\mathbf{u}^{(e)}(t)\bigr)^\top \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}^{(-e)}, \quad \hat y(t_0) = \bar{y}_0^{(-e)} & \text{predict year } e \text{ from its drivers} \end{array} $$ Only the drivers of the left-out year enter the prediction. The error is the root-mean-square error (RMSE, t/ha) over whole trajectories, on a fixed day, and at maturity. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r ## Each year is predicted by a model fitted to the other years of the same ## genotype, starting from the mean initial biomass of those years. ## Returns P[genotype, year, day]. cross_validate <- function(Theta, tr, fit, genotypes = tr$genotypes) { P <- array(NA_real_, dim(tr$Y)) S <- length(tr$years) for (g in match(genotypes, tr$genotypes)) { d <- make_design(Theta, tr, tr$genotypes[g]) coef <- t(sapply(seq_len(S), function(v) { train <- d$year != v fit(d$X[train, ], d$dy[train]) })) y0 <- (sum(tr$Y[g, , 1]) - tr$Y[g, , 1]) / (S - 1) P[g, , ] <- t(simulate(coef, Theta, y0)) } P } ## RMSE over whole trajectories, on a fixed day (array index; 99 is day 113 ## after sowing) and at maturity. Genotypes that were not predicted are ignored. evaluate <- function(P, tr, fixed_day = 99) { err <- P - tr$Y err[, , 1] <- NA # the initial value is given last <- cbind(as.vector(row(tr$nend)), as.vector(col(tr$nend)), as.vector(tr$nend) + 1) rmse <- function(e) sqrt(mean(e^2, na.rm = TRUE)) c(trajectory_rmse = rmse(err), fixed_day_rmse = rmse(err[, , fixed_day]), maturity_rmse = rmse(err[last])) } ``` ## Python ```python # Each year is predicted by a model fitted to the other years of the same # genotype, starting from the mean initial biomass of those years. # Returns P[genotype, year, day]. def cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit, genotypes=None): P = np.full(tr.Y.shape, np.nan) S = len(tr.years) for g in (tr.genotypes if genotypes is None else genotypes): i = list(tr.genotypes).index(g) d = make_design(Theta, tr, g) coef = np.array([fit(d.X[d.year != s], d.dy[d.year != s]) for s in range(S)]) y0 = (tr.Y[i, :, 0].sum() - tr.Y[i, :, 0]) / (S - 1) P[i] = simulate(coef, Theta.array, y0) return P # RMSE over whole trajectories, on a fixed day (days after sowing) and at # maturity. Genotypes that were not predicted are ignored. def evaluate(P, tr, fixed_day=113): err = P - tr.Y err[:, :, 0] = np.nan # the initial value is given g, s = np.indices(tr.nend.shape) def rmse(e): return np.sqrt(np.nanmean(e ** 2)) return {"trajectory_rmse": rmse(err), "fixed_day_rmse": rmse(err[:, :, fixed_day - tr.das0]), "maturity_rmse": rmse(err[g, s, tr.nend])} ``` ::: The sparse model (STLSQ) for all 199 genotypes: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} P <- cached("cv_stlsq.rds", cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq)) round(evaluate(P, tr), 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python P = cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq) print({k: round(float(v), 3) for k, v in evaluate(P, tr).items()}) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` trajectory_rmse fixed_day_rmse maturity_rmse 0.449 0.565 0.688 ``` ::: ::: ## Predicted trajectories Held-out predictions of the sparse model, for genotypes spread over the ranking of final biomass and for selected years. Thick lines: APSIM; thin lines: model. Switch genotypes and years on and off. The right panel shows the growth rate of the same curves, estimated by centered differences. ```{ojs} //| echo: false d3 = window.d3 Plot = window.Plot traj = FileAttachment("data/interactive/trajectories.json").json() shades = ["#8B1E3F", "#00A6D6", "#014E81", "#6D8B1E", "#6B7280"] viewof genos = toggles("Genotypes", traj.genotypes, shades, [traj.genotypes[0], traj.genotypes[2], traj.genotypes[4]]) viewof years = toggles("Years", [1983, 1989, 1998, 2008], ["#374151", "#374151", "#374151", "#374151"], [1989, 1998, 2008]) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false { const rows = genos.flatMap(name => years.flatMap(year => { const g = traj.genotypes.indexOf(name), s = traj.years.indexOf(year); return ["observed", "model"].flatMap(source => traj[source][g][s].map((y, i, a) => ({ name, year, source, das: traj.das0 + i, y, rate: i > 0 && i < a.length - 1 ? (a[i + 1] - a[i - 1]) / 2 : null}))); })); const panel = (key, label, domain) => Plot.plot({ width: 262, height: 70 + 120 * years.length, marginLeft: 42, marginRight: 8, style: {fontSize: "10px"}, x: {label: "days after sowing"}, y: {label, domain}, fy: {label: null, domain: years, tickFormat: d => d}, color: {domain: traj.genotypes, range: shades}, marks: [ Plot.line(rows.filter(d => d.source === "observed" && d[key] !== null), {x: "das", y: key, fy: "year", z: "name", stroke: "name", strokeWidth: 4, strokeOpacity: 0.3}), Plot.line(rows.filter(d => d.source === "model" && d[key] !== null), {x: "das", y: key, fy: "year", z: "name", stroke: "name", strokeWidth: 1.4}) ] }); return html`

d$pred)^2)) ggplot(d, aes(obs, pred, colour = year)) + geom_abline(colour = dgxe[["grey"]], linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.5) + annotate("text", x = min(d$obs), y = max(d$pred), hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.4, label = sprintf("RMSE %.2f t/ha", rmse)) + scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c(dgxe[["blue"]], dgxe[["cyan"]], dgxe[["burgundy"]]), name = "year") + coord_equal() + labs(x = "APSIM biomass at maturity (t/ha)", y = "predicted biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() + theme(legend.position = "right") ``` ::: ## Python ```python from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap g, s = np.indices(tr.nend.shape) obs, pred = tr.Y[g, s, tr.nend].ravel(), P[g, s, tr.nend].ravel() year = np.tile(tr.years, len(tr.genotypes)) rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((obs - pred) ** 2)) colours = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("dgxe", [BLUE, CYAN, BURGUNDY]) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.6, 4)) ax.plot([obs.min(), obs.max()], [obs.min(), obs.max()], color="#9CA3AF", lw=0.8) points = ax.scatter(obs, pred, c=year, s=4, alpha=0.5, cmap=colours, linewidths=0) ax.text(0.04, 0.95, f"RMSE {rmse:.2f} t/ha", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top") ax.set_aspect("equal") ax.set_xlabel("APSIM biomass at maturity (t/ha)") ax.set_ylabel("predicted biomass (t/ha)") fig.colorbar(points, label="year", shrink=0.8) fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-validate_files/figure-html/05-3-run-1.png){width=720} ::: ::: ## Comparison of fitting methods All methods of step 4 are evaluated in the same way: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scores <- cached("cv_methods.rds", t(sapply(fit_methods, function(fit) { evaluate(cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit), tr) }))) round(scores, 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python scores = pd.DataFrame({name: evaluate(cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit), tr) for name, fit in fit_methods.items()}).T print(scores.round(3)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` trajectory_rmse fixed_day_rmse maturity_rmse OLS 0.449 0.563 0.692 ridge 0.451 0.578 0.679 lasso 0.456 0.589 0.680 elastic net 0.455 0.588 0.679 best subset (k = 8) 0.466 0.613 0.685 backward (k = 8) 0.467 0.610 0.698 STLSQ 0.449 0.565 0.688 ``` ::: ::: The methods are close to each other. The sparse models use fewer terms for a similar error. ## Number of terms For a library that also contains products of pairs of drivers (`pairs = TRUE`, 136 terms), the held-out error of backward elimination (every twentieth genotype) as a function of the number of terms is: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Theta2 <- make_library(drv, pairs = TRUE) genotypes <- tr$genotypes[seq(1, 199, by = 20)] ks <- c(4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 60, 136) by_k <- cached("rmse_vs_k.rds", data.frame(k = ks, rmse = sapply(ks, function(k) { fit <- function(X, dy) fit_subset(X, dy, k, "backward") evaluate(cross_validate(Theta2, tr, fit, genotypes), tr)[[1]] }))) ``` ::: ## Python ```python Theta2 = make_library(drv, pairs=True) genotypes = tr.genotypes[::20] ks = [4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 60, 136] def rmse_for(k): def fit(X, dy): return fit_subset(X, dy, k, "backward") return evaluate(cross_validate(Theta2, tr, fit, genotypes), tr)["trajectory_rmse"] by_k = pd.DataFrame({"k": ks, "rmse": [rmse_for(k) for k in ks]}) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(by_k, aes(k, rmse)) + geom_line(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 2) + labs(x = "number of terms (136-term library)", y = "held-out trajectory RMSE (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() ``` ::: ## Python ```python fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 2.8)) ax.plot(by_k["k"], by_k["rmse"], "o-", color=BLUE) ax.set_xlabel("number of terms (136-term library)") ax.set_ylabel("held-out trajectory RMSE (t/ha)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-validate_files/figure-html/05-8-run-1.png){width=720} ::: :::
